campaign: MOSS in overgo does what the MOSS Ultra workflow does in ComfyUI, each section held to ComfyUI's recording

items.title: A MOSS step's time is read between the completed steps of one draw, so the check measures no estimate below nothing

steps.title: A MOSS step's time is read between the completed steps of one draw, so the check measures no estimate below nothing
steps.rationale:
SQA-520 (P2), checked by the lead against internal/latentimage/step_time_windows_model_test.go and the run at efa59bd59: valid, observed (the models lane failed it after all five draws, a request's own part read as -717 ms). It costs measured time: a failed lane ends the cycle before its cells. The check reads a guided step as the difference of two requests' walls divided by four and a request's own part as what is left of the 2-step wall, so two draws that vary by more than the estimate make it negative; the run's draws went beside another process on the card, which widened that spread. The change: a guided step and a pass are read between completed steps of one draw (processmeasure.WithSteps, which the sampler already tells), a request's own part as its first step's excess over a step, and the kernel launches and bytes to the card as before; the 4-step draw, there only to fit and cross-check the estimate, goes. First read how the sampler tells processmeasure.Stepped and ComfyUI's step reading.

Check: TestWhereAMossStepsTimeGoes on the card.

Note: files set to internal/latentimage: the step that replaces do, whose check named a clock (TestNoClockEndsWorkInsideTheMachine), writes the test do would have

decisions.question: skill.md's 227 rule lines each cite a check. Read at 3ba4de8c7: the first check of 181 has a doc comment and of 45 has none, and the comments state what their test holds, not the rule that cites it ("purpose = recursive self-improvement ..." cites TestCycleFilesDeclinesAndAcceptsNothing, whose comment is the cycle's comparisons; "scorecard columns = ..." cites TestScorecardRowsEveryServableModel, whose comment is rows and dashes). Writing skill.md from the comments as they stand changes what it says. Which form does skill.md take?
options: Each rule line moves onto its first check as a doc-comment line of its own, and skill.md is generated from those lines and its judgement section, so it says what it says now, each rule written once on its check
skill.md holds its terms and judgement lines alone; the rule lines go, each check saying its rule when it refuses
skill.md is written from the tests' doc comments as they stand, its wording changing to theirs
decisions.recommendation: Each rule line moves onto its first check as a doc-comment line of its own, and skill.md is generated from those lines and its judgement section, so it says what it says now, each rule written once on its check
